svg.text: increaseticks() — Deciding When a New Millisecond Is Due
src/dosbox.cpp — the real-time gate behind TIMER_AddTick() and the cycles=auto adjuster (Ch.3 §3.9)
(no new host millisecond has elapsed yet)
avoids resonating with the host's own
↩ returns to Normal_Loop — no tick this pass
this is the ordinary path — Ch.3 §3.9
(enough data for a full ~250 ms measurement window)
(rules out noise / another app briefly stealing the host CPU)
— plus extra caps under sustained high CPU_CycleMax
runs either way — next window starts fresh
increaseticks() decides *when* a millisecond is due; CPU_CycleMax decides *how much* CPU work fits inside it.
Only the green paths hand real work onward — a tick budget, or a revised CPU_CycleMax. Every other path changes nothing.
Turbo mode (top right) never asks whether real host time has passed at all — see Ch.3 §3.9.
The emergency downscale (left) is the only update path that skips the ticksDone/ticksScheduled reset.
